candidate.blueprint_locator: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control: identify fall hazards, implement environmental safety measures, use appropriate assistive supports and prevent injury in high-risk clients.
candidate.blueprint_topic: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — older-adult home fall prevention
candidate.educational_objective: Reduce home fall risk in older adults by removing trip hazards, improving lighting, installing grab bars/railings as needed, and supporting safe activity rather than environmental hazards or unnecessary immobility.

options.A: Limit routine walking inside the home so the older adult has fewer opportunities to experience a fall.
options.B: Remove tripping hazards, improve lighting, and install bathroom grab bars or other appropriate home-safety supports.
options.C: Keep familiar throw rugs in walking paths while adding brighter lighting to improve visual contrast.
options.D: Use loose backless slippers indoors because they are easier to remove if balance is lost.

candidate.rationale: Current CDC older-adult fall-prevention guidance recommends making the home safer by removing things that can be tripped over, improving lighting, installing grab bars in and around the tub or shower and next to the toilet, and adding stair railings. CDC also encourages strength and balance activity rather than unnecessary restriction of routine movement. Therefore B is correct. A promotes avoidable inactivity, C leaves a known tripping hazard in place, and D uses insecure footwear that can worsen fall risk.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Older-adult home fall prevention includes removing trip hazards such as throw rugs/clutter, improving lighting and installing bathroom grab bars/other supports; routine safe mobility should not be restricted solely to reduce opportunities to fall.
candidate.source_document_title: Preventing Falls and Hip Fractures; Information for Older Adults
candidate.source_locator: Preventing a fall or hip fracture > Make your home safer: get rid of trip hazards, add bathroom grab bars, railings on both sides of stairs, improve lighting. Strength and balance exercises are also recommended. Information for Older Adults explicitly identifies throw rugs as trip hazards and recommends brighter lighting and bathroom grab bars.
